clause.quote: Given a local or remote event, a non-controller, non-witness, non-delegator validator MUST first verify the event's controller signatures, witness signatures (if witnessed), and delegator anchoring seal (if delegated) before it can accept that event into its copy of that event's KEL.

inferred_from.inference: The sentence states what a validator must verify before it can accept an event, not that it must accept one that passes. No sentence obliges a validator to accept anything, so that a validator should accept an event that passes every check, and that the event is then on the trunk, is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, KERI, What MUST means here).

clause.quote: In KERI, there MUST be at most one valid KEL for any identifier or none at all.

inferred_from.inference: With rule A2 ("An interaction event may not supersede any event."), this says a validator should not accept an event that is not a rotation where a different event already lies on the trunk. Neither sentence carries a keyword, so refusing it is graded SHOULD, and the state it leaves is graded at the same level.
inferred_from.quote: Notably, an event that may not supersede, according to the rules below, another event at the same location cannot be first seen at all by that KEL.

description: An inception and an interaction, then a different interaction at the same sequence number, also signed by the current key. A second interaction cannot supersede the first (rule A2), so a validator should not accept it, and its key state stays at the first interaction.
title: Conflicting interaction, validly signed
